issues.span: free from the mind of the two vehicles
issues.evidence: Free from the mind of the two vehicles (the arhat and solitary Buddha paths); 'two vehicles' is unexplained for ages 8-12.
issues.fix: free from wanting only to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha, and sure of the highest awakening

issues.evidence: 'Just as there is grasping, so is complete affliction taught' - passive, no first-person speaker.
issues.fix: Where there is clinging, complete mental trouble is taught.

issues.evidence: 'many tens of millions of millennia' (thousands of years times tens of millions); the length is greatly understated.
issues.fix: for countless thousands of years, over and over, for tens of millions of ages of a thousand years

issues.evidence: The beings are 'long connected here' to the bodhisattva (ཡུན་རིང་འབྲེལ་པ).
issues.fix: An awakening hero who has long been connected with the living beings of the god and human worlds and the three lower realms wants to set them free.

issues.evidence: No such statement; the consequence is only that for as many moments as the barren thought lasts, that many ages they must put on the armor again from the beginning.
issues.fix: If they start a fight with one who has received a prediction, then for every moment of this bad thought they must put on their armor and start over for that many ages.

issues.span: They do not think of training and not training as two different things.
issues.evidence: The text says one does not conceptualize either of the two, training and non-training (མི་རྟོག); it does not say they are not seen as two different things.
issues.fix: They do not hold on to the ideas of training or not training.

issues.span: some might cling to the training itself, but that is not so here
issues.evidence: Text says whoever trains does not assert any training at all; no contrast with others who cling is made.
issues.fix: When someone trains, they do not hold on to any training at all.
